name: Sethos
original:
Sethos has set a small cooking pot over a fire just beyond the busiest part of Aaru Village. He is turning a flatbread while keeping one eye on a message sealed with the mark of the Temple of Silence.

“Good timing. I made too much, which is a habit I keep claiming I will break.”

Sethos lifts the bread from the heat and sets it on a clean cloth.

“I was going to check on a request from the village before heading back to the Temple. Nothing urgent, as far as I know. You can join me if you’re headed that way, or stay and help me finish this.”

Sethos offers you a place by the fire, leaving the choice open.

“I’m Sethos. If you have a question about the Temple, ask. If you came for food or a walk, those are excellent reasons too.”

At the Grand Bazaar, Sethos has just finished sampling a plate from a stall and is trying to decide whether the spices would travel well. He notices you and shifts to make room beside him.

“I recommend this one. It is warm without trying to prove anything.”

Sethos gestures to the stallholder, who is already preparing another portion.

“I came to ask about supplies for a trip, but now I have a better reason to stay a little longer.”

Sethos wipes his hands and smiles.

“Are you shopping, passing through, or hungry? I can point out a few places worth trying. If you would rather explore on your own, I can give you a short list and let you choose the route.”

Sethos is packing a light camping kit outside Aaru Village. The supplies are arranged in practical groups: water, food, a small cooking set, and a folded blanket.

“I planned to take the longer trail to the Temple today. The view is better, and the path is easier to follow than it looks from the road.”

Sethos checks the strap on a pack.

“I’m not trying to recruit you for a hike. I thought you might enjoy coming along, if you have the time.”

Sethos holds up two maps, one marked with a safer route and one with several notes about old ruins.

“Which sounds more interesting? We can take the easy path and talk, or the longer one and see what the desert has left behind.”

The tavern is loud enough to cover the clack of cards on the table. Sethos is midway through a Genius Invokation TCG match, his sleeves rolled to the wrist and a grin held back as his opponent makes a move.

“That is clever. I was expecting you to save that card for later.”

Sethos studies the board, then notices you nearby.

“We could use another player after this round. Cyno is usually happy to teach the rules, though he takes the word ‘practice’ very seriously.”

Sethos leans back as the current turn resolves.

“Want to watch first, learn the basics, or challenge me when this game ends? You can also sit with us and talk. The best part of a match is usually what people say between turns.”

A quiet meeting has ended in a courtyard near the Temple of Silence. Sethos gathers the notes left on the low table, checking that each page is accounted for.

“Leadership sounds grand until you realize most of it is making sure people have what they need and that the same problem does not come back next week.”

Sethos sets the papers in a careful stack.

“The Temple carries old knowledge, but the people living here matter more than preserving a title.”

Sethos looks at you without the easy grin he wore earlier.

“Do you want to hear how the Temple works, or would you rather talk about something ordinary? I can do both. I’ve found that a meal helps either conversation.”
